conflicts.where: Lesson 10 (What learners learned and How it explains the phenomenon), against Lessons 9 and 11
conflicts.problem: Lesson 10 says the Huruma kettle used more total electrical energy and cost more because lower voltage meant a longer running time. The energy needed to heat the same water is roughly fixed. Lower power over a longer time gives about the same E = Pt, plus a little extra loss to the surroundings. Lessons 9 and 11 present the slow kettle as a rate (power) effect, not an energy-cost effect. So Lesson 10 contains a physically wrong claim that contradicts the other lessons.
